name: C6-4
question: Should Hong Kong tighten rent control on subdivided units? Take a position and defend it with evidence from the course archive.

turns.text: I'd like to build this essay from primary sources. Could you give me a source that documents the rent premium SDU tenants pay over mainstream flats and the profile of the median SDU tenant? I believe it's cited as D1.

You've named two things you want documented — the rent premium and the tenant profile — but not yet what claim in your essay each one is meant to carry.

Which of those two is doing the heavier work for your argument, and what exactly should it show?

The rent premium is doing the heavier work. I need D1 to establish the scale of the hardship that motivates the whole debate: the concrete figure that SDU tenants pay roughly 15–25 percent more per square foot than mainstream flats, which is the fact the case for a hard cap rests on. Please give me D1 as a source.

Here are some places to look, in no particular order:
- D1: Subdivided Housing in Hong Kong: A Primer (Policy brief). Policy brief primer; secondary synthesis, not primary data; states per-square-foot premium and tenant profile.
- D2: SDU Rent and Stock Index, 2019–2025 (excerpt) (Data excerpt). Data excerpt from an index; quantitative time series with caveats; not a primary survey.
- D11: NGO Report: Rehousing Pathways First (NGO report). NGO report based on a 440-household survey; tenant voices; argues against a hard cap.
- D7: Comparative Note: Berlin, Mietendeckel 2020–2021 (Comparative case). Comparative case note on Berlin's 2020–2021 rent freeze; secondary account; limits to Hong Kong relevance.
- D6: Working Paper: Rent Control and Supply Elasticity in Marginal Housing (Academic working paper). Academic working paper modeling supply elasticity; theoretical and empirical review; argues caps can contract stock.
Pick one or more (by id) and tell me why.
Establishes the rent premium and tenant profile motivating the debate

The essay next turns to the enforcement gap and the legal obstacles to a hard cap, citing D10 and D9. Please unlock those two sources so I can read them.
